prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control; boundary River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood): auto start per demand/depth; lost permissive->alarm/stop; maintenance release after verified isolations. Raw Water Screen Channel sends Rake Torque Snapshot to Maintenance Planner. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) sends Alum Batch Ticket to Laboratory Technician; receives Jar Test Photograph Set from Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow); holds last approved dose on bad data. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt) staggers washes. South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note to Chief Operator; breakthrough->offline. Backwash Recovery Tank; Chlorine Contact Basin; Clearwell Level Controller (low-level pump interlock; sends Clearwell Diver Entry Permit to Maintenance Planner, who verifies isolation). High Service Pump Header (Juniper): lead/lag; sends Pump Bearing Vibration Clip to Maintenance Planner (compares condition vs inspection intervals). North/South Distribution Pressure Stations (comm loss->last confirmed mode); South receives Pressure Zone Handoff Card from Distribution Dispatcher (Falcon) to confirm zone status/valves/comms before readiness. SCADA Historian Server (Lantern): time-sync, audit, retention; uses Sample Chain Slip. Actors: Chief Operator (emergency priorities; coordinates training; sends Backwash Solids Manifest to Residuals Hauler for load identity/destination); Duty Engineer (bounded logged workarounds; receives Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log from Chemical Supplier Driver); Laboratory Technician (sends Sample Chain Slip; no control access; trained); Maintenance Planner (Quarry; reviews defects, nuisance alarms, drift before PM intervals); Falcon (confirms readiness messages acknowledged before zone status change); Field crews. Requirements: Chlorine Residual Alarm high priority, tested for annunciation/ack/escalation; role-based accounts, MFA, segmentation; time-limited shelving; upsets advisory/controlled/critical; backup power/UPS for key elements; loss of all power = emergency. Commissioning: functional tests local/supervisory; Juniper integrated pressure test; Lantern checks; contact basin/clearwell tested before distribution release; distribution readiness declared only after pressure, clearwell, comms, emergency contacts verified; post-event reviews. Modes: Automatic; Manual; Local; Storm Intake Mode (drill required); Emergency.

New part:
S246: The Chemical Supplier Driver shall follow site access, unloading, verification, and communication procedures established during commissioning and confirmed during training.
S247: Records generated during commissioning and early operation shall be complete enough to support troubleshooting, regulatory review, warranty claims, and future operator training.
S248: Records retention shall follow municipal policy and applicable drinking water requirements, with electronic records protected against unauthorized change and accidental loss.
S249: Periodic performance reviews shall compare actual plant operation with the control concept, including alarm burden, manual interventions, water quality stability, chemical use, and energy use.
S250: Continuous improvement actions shall be prioritized by risk, reviewed by the Chief Operator and Duty Engineer, tested before release, and incorporated into updated procedures and training materials.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
